title: A run must record how it was started so it can be restarted
description:
Restarting epic-dha under the same run id took five attempts today, each failing on a different missing piece of the invocation, because nothing records how the run was started:

1. no executor: ticfac-exec-subprocess was not beside the binary
2. no code-hosting surface: GITHUB_TOKEN unset
3. died: adopted attempt of e9n names executor 'herdr'; this is local-subprocess — no -profiles
4. same, after guessing HERDR_ENV and HERDR_SOCKET_PATH
5. same, after -profiles profiles — the repo has BOTH profiles/ (local-subprocess) and profiles-herdr/ (herdr), and only the second matches the run's own evidence

Each refusal was individually clear and fail-closed, which is right. The problem is that none of them could be anticipated: the flags, env and profile directory a run was started with are nowhere in its durable state, so resuming a run is archaeology against its own evidence files. The provenance block in gate evidence records profile_digest, executor and model AFTER the fact; the invocation that produced them is not recorded at all.

The run already writes run.log, events.jsonl and a checkpoint. It should write the invocation too: argv, the resolved profiles directory, the executor per role, and which environment variables it depended on (by name, never value — this repo is public). Then a restart is 'ticfac run-epic -run-id epic-dha --as-before' or at minimum a printed command a person can paste.

This is the same class as the missing test failure messages atn fixed: a system that knows the answer and does not say it, leaving the reader to re-derive it.
acceptance_criteria: A stopped run can be restarted from its own durable state without a person reconstructing the invocation, proven by a test that starts a run, stops it, and restarts it from what it recorded
